Bio: Most people leave a health check-up with a report they never open again.I've spent the last 4+ years at Zoī trying to fix that, from the inside.I started by building the medical and operational foundation: clinical quality, physician workflows, research infrastructure from scratch. Then I moved into product, because the hardest part was never the diagnosis. It's the 12 months after. Turning a complex medical workup into a roadmap a person actually follows requires making the physician's needs and the patient's reality converge. That's a product problem.Doing this well means making very different worlds talk to each other, clinicians, engineers and the business, and building the team and the expert network that turn a clinical idea into something real. That's been as much of my job as the product itself.As CPO, I lead both surfaces: Codex, our physician-facing software, and the member app that turns a medical diagnosis into clear actions, visible progress, and measurable behavior change over 12 months. Two very different users, one coherent system.AI sits at the core of how I build and how I work. I'm building AI-native products, including an in-app assistant designed with EU MDR compliance as a hard constraint. And I instrument my own job with it: my discovery system is maintained by agents that mine the sources, extract and classify frictions, reorder the opportunity tree and flag breaks in the evidence → problem → solution chain. Same for my research sweeps and my editorial pipeline. Not experiments, systems in production, built without being an engineer.I'm also one of our own patients. That keeps me honest about where the gap between data and real life actually lives.
